sentences.text: The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — includes parts of the skull and a left lower jaw from one young animal.
Albalophosaurus was described in 2009 from fossils found in 1997 in the Kuwajima Formation of central Japan.
The original authors classified Albalophosaurus as Cerapoda incertae sedis and did not consider it a ceratopsian.
The exact age of the strata is unknown, but the Kuwajima Formation likely formed during the Early Cretaceous, possibly after the Berriasian and before the Barremian.
Recent studies suggest the Kuwajima Formation is most likely from the Valanginian to Hauterivian, though the exact age remains uncertain.
The Paleobiology Database records the time range of Albalophosaurus as the Barremian, between 125.77 and 121.4 million years ago.
